purpose: Validate the dev.7 onboarding and repair file path on the attached SparkFun RP2350 XRP without movement.

network_profile_after_repair.reason: The laptop remained on Pink rather than joining the XRP hotspot. The profile and address were read over USB.

observations.detail: The first attached-device pass updated only four stale release files and verified all 23 destinations.

Two temporary root files confirmed that os.rename(source, existing_destination) replaces the destination on this RP2350 filesystem. Temporary files were removed. Browser and command-line repair now verify the temporary payload and activate it with that single rename rather than deleting the working file first.
A second comment-only alteration exercised the revised single-rename activation path on the physical board.
ucsb_xrp, ucsb_xrp_service.service, and XRPLib.board imported after repair with the expected versions.
The final USB session ended with a controller reset; the serial device re-enumerated.

browser_boundary.detail: The public wizard reached the native macOS project-folder chooser in the user's Chrome. The operating-system chooser appeared outside the controlled tab and was not automated further. The exact manifest, comparison, raw-REPL installation semantics, imports, reset, and network-profile read were exercised against the attached board through the equivalent command-line transport.

firmware.reason: The attached controller already reported the exact pinned RP2350 MicroPython runtime; rewriting correct firmware would add no evidence. Firmware integrity and volume behavior remain covered by the browser harness.
